original_question: Let α be a free, probability-measure-preserving action of F2. Is there a free probability-measure-preserving action β such that Eα = Eβ and every nontrivial element of F2 acts ergodically in β?
target_in_paper: Section 13 (Wei Dai), Problem 45(ii) (attributed there to Miller–Tserunyan), read together with the setup sentence of Problem 45 and the orbit-equivalence clause in Problem 45(i). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2507.03972))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the main mathematical core: the group F_2, a free p.m.p. action α, the search for another free p.m.p. action β with the same orbit equivalence relation, and the strengthened requirement that every nonidentity element act ergodically in β. That is very close to the intent of Problem 45(ii), once the paper’s surrounding setup is made explicit. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2507.03972))
missing_details: The paper assumes from the outset that α is not just free and p.m.p., but also ergodic. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2507.03972))

The actions are stated on a measure space (X, μ); to make the question stand-alone, β should also be specified as an action of F_2 on the same probability space (X, μ). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2507.03972))

The notation E_α and E_β should be defined explicitly as the orbit equivalence relations of α and β. This is used in Problem 45(i) and is needed to make the reformulated question self-contained. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2507.03972))

The phrase “every nontrivial element of F_2 acts ergodically in β” should be spelled out as: for every x ∈ F_2 \ {e}, the individual measure-preserving transformation β(x) is ergodic on (X, μ). ([tianyuan.amss.ac.cn](https://tianyuan.amss.ac.cn/upload/fab78d36-bd52-42eb-84d3-ff99c953bb08/20250708/67111751937959724.pdf?utm_source=openai))

Your draft blends the all-elements conclusion from Problem 45(ii) with the orbit-equivalence condition made explicit in Problem 45(i); that dependence on nearby context should be made explicit in the final stand-alone version. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2507.03972))
refined_question: Let α: F_2 ↷ (X, μ) be a free, probability-measure-preserving, ergodic action, and let E_α denote its orbit equivalence relation. Does there exist a free, probability-measure-preserving action β: F_2 ↷ (X, μ) such that E_β = E_α and, for every nonidentity element x ∈ F_2, the transformation β(x) is ergodic on (X, μ)?
justification: The draft is aiming at the Miller–Tserunyan part of Problem 45, but it omits the standing hypothesis that α is ergodic and relies on nearby context to carry the orbit-equivalence condition. In Section 13, Problem 45 first fixes a free, p.m.p., ergodic action α of F_2 on (X, μ), then in part (i) asks for an orbit-equivalent β making a prescribed nonidentity element x act ergodically, and then in part (ii) asks the stronger all-nontrivial-elements version. So the sharpest stand-alone paper-faithful rewrite is the orbit-equivalent, all-elements-ergodic formulation above. The paper does not supply an explicit equivalent reformulation of this stronger question. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2507.03972))
